provenance.source: NECB 2025 Division B: Tables 3.2.2.2, 3.2.2.3, 3.2.2.4 (doors, split out in 2025), 3.2.3.1, Article 3.2.1.4 — retrieved via the building-codes MCP server (necb:2025). ALL VALUES VERIFIED IDENTICAL to NECB 2020 (opaque/fenestration/ground tables byte-match; 2025 door table equals the 2020 door row). Performance-path articles renumbered 8.4.4.x -> 8.4.5.x (verbatim text).
provenance.note: Runtime never contacts the MCP. U-values are EFFECTIVE transmittance per 3.1.1.7.

ground_floor_extent.note: Table 3.2.3.1 floors row reads '0.757 for 1.2 m' in zones 4-7B — a perimeter strip per 3.2.3.3.(3); the slab FIELD carries no prescriptive maximum below zone 8 — vs '0.379 for full area' in zone 8. The strip/full-area U is the u_values.ground.floor bin at the building HDD (u_values itself is structurally pinned to the legacy JSON, so the extent lives here). Verified against the printed table via the codes MCP (necb 2020 and 2025 identical).

fdwr.text: FDWR = 0.40 for HDD <= 4000; FDWR = (2000 - 0.2 x HDD)/3000 for 4000 < HDD < 7000; FDWR = 0.20 for HDD >= 7000
fdwr.boundary_note: Code text says <= 4000 -> 0.40; legacy openstudio-standards uses < 4000 with the linear branch at exactly 4000 — identical result ((2000-800)/3000 = 0.40).

srr_max.text: The total skylight area shall be less than 2% of the gross roof area

hdd_bins_note: keys are HDD bin CEILINGS {3000,4000,5000,6000,7000,9999} = zones 4/5/6/7A/7B/8; lookup rule (legacy-exact): first value where hdd < key, fallback 0.110

reference_envelope.note: populated fully in P4 (lightweight layers from Note A-8.4.4.4.(1), air leakage from 8.4.3.3.(3))

article_coverage.note: Envelope-slice coverage; statuses flip as phases land.

articles.title: General — envelope components accounted
articles.how: Envelope components accounted per the prescriptive Section 3.2 requirements via the reference transform (8.4.5.3./8.4.5.4.: U-values at the building HDD, FDWR/SRR, lightweight construction) — the realization of 8.4.1.1.(1) for the envelope slice.

articles.title: Air Leakage
articles.how: The (2) I_AGW operating-pressure conversion of the 75 Pa leakage rate is computed and applied per space in the reference air-leakage default (apply_air_leakage_default, which cites this article); (1) accounting happens through the infiltration objects on both models.
